newsitem.title: GERMANY: AMB says not planning five-mark share soon.
newsitem.headline: AMB says not planning five-mark share soon.

text.p: German insurance group Aachener und Muenchener Beteiligungs AG, known as AMB, on Friday said it had no immediate plans to reduce the par value of its shares to five marks ($3.37) from 50 marks.

AMB Chairman Wolfgang Kaske told the insurer's annual general meeting that AMB would have the technical capability to switch to a five mark share next year but that the move did not make sense before the move to a single European currency.
Kaske added that it would be more expensive for AMB to cut its par value than for other companies because 80 percent of its stock was registered.

Many large German companies have taken advantage of a legal change to move their shares to a lower par value in recent months in a bid to attract more foreign investors and improve their stock's liquidity.
The switch, the equivalent of a 10-for-one stock split, cuts the price of shares to about one tenth of their price before the split.
AMB bearer shares closed on Friday at 1,140 marks.
